_comment: Manual overrides for the 1836 start converter (tools/convert_history.ps1). Each rule targets a vanilla BASE building key, optionally scoped to a country (region_state tag, e.g. 'GBR') and/or state (e.g. 'STATE_HOME_COUNTIES'). action: 'force_tier' sets the factory to tier N (1-based) regardless of its vanilla PM; 'force_industry_tier' re-tiers it onto ANOTHER config industry's tier N (fields: industry, tier) — needed when the target chain is a separate industry whose base building never appears in vanilla history (the steamer chain); 'remove' deletes the factory from the start. Precedence: most specific scope wins (country+state > country > state > none); ties resolved by last rule. Only the 'rules' array is read; '_examples' is ignored. See config/start_baseline.json (generated by tools/extract_start.ps1) for the inventory of what exists to target.
_why_steamer_seed: REVERTED (user-ruled 2026-08-16, same day): the seed existed only to feed the abnormal from-start steam-port construction, which F66 traced to the engine provisioning every overseas state once per port building TYPE — the disease to fix, not the symptom to feed. The force_industry_tier machinery stays (documented, tested); the rules are withdrawn. The five rules it carried: GBR Home Counties 5 / FRA Brittany 4 / USA Virginia 2 / BEL Flanders 1 / PRU West Prussia 1 -> building_shipyard_metal.
_why_chain_seed: THE §2 CHAIN SEED — RATIFIED STANDING DESIGN (user-ruled 2026-08-16 late evening, §10.60.3: 'on start, the t1 steam ports and steamyards must be provided'; originally user-directed the same evening after the graded-port probe measured ZERO metal shipyards world-wide in 15 years against standing steamer demand from the engine-provisioned stubs): every LEADER-OWNED anchorage in the GBR and FRA 1836 markets (the two markets whose leader holds screw_frigate from day 0 - tier-1 starting techs are GBR/FRA/USA/PRU/BEL, of whom only GBR and FRA have overseas empires) becomes a tier-2 (t1 steam, graded 1/10-size) port stub at level 1 (the anchorage clamp holds it there), and each leader gets ONE metal shipyard by converting a small clipper-shipyard block (GBR East Anglia 3 lv, FRA Brittany 1 lv - the clipper-capacity loss is the accepted price). LEADER-OWNED ONLY by landmine L14: subject-owned anchorages (BIC/SIL/ION/NSW/...) would start with a building their own technologies cannot unlock - preflight caught it on the first dry run; their stubs arrive from the engine when they research. STEEL IS NOT SEEDED: both leaders already hold 1836 steel mills (GBR Yorkshire 6 lv, FRA Alsace 1 lv). Q5c RULED (user, 2026-08-16 night): FRA holds atmospheric_engine from the tier-1 starting grant, so it is GRANTED one motor factory - the Rhone 1-level paper mill (Lyon; FRA keeps 4 paper levels elsewhere) converts to motor t1 (40 engines/wk at full staffing vs the yard s 16.6 need; eats 22.8 steel/wk beside Alsace s 65). KNOWN LIMPS, accepted per the stop-there rule (coal/iron by market), and leader-owned overseas BASIC-port states (Malta/Gibraltar/Malaya) are NOT seeded - the engine provisions their steam stubs within weeks at graded cost (measured, ports-graded-probe). 13 port seeds (GBR 7, FRA 6) + 2 yard conversions + 1 FRA motor conversion (Q5c); regenerate with the gen_seed_rules.mjs pattern (vanilla history anchorages x ui/presets.js market membership).
